BIRMINGHAM, Ala. (WBRC) - FIRST ALERT WEATHER DAYS: Your First Alert Weather Team has declared First Alert Weather Days today through Saturday for dangerous heat. Temperatures will climb into the upper 90s, with heat indices reaching 105+ degrees. A heat advisory will go into effect at 11 a.m. and will expire by 8 p.m. on Saturday. With a busy Labor Day weekend ahead, make sure you are staying hydrated and keeping an eye on the forecast, especially if you are heading to a football game or spending extended time outside.
THE NEXT 24 HOURS: We are starting warm and muggy again this morning, with temperatures in the 70s. Highs will surge into the upper 90s this afternoon, putting us near record-breaking levels. The records to beat today are 98 degrees in Birmingham set in 2011, 100 degrees in Tuscaloosa set in 2011, and 97 degrees in Anniston set in 1957. At best, a very isolated shower or storm could pop up during the peak heating of the day, but rain chances remain at 20% or less.
LABOR DAY WEEKEND: The prolonged stretch of dangerous heat continues through Saturday. High temperatures remain in the mid-to-upper 90s each afternoon, while the humidity pushes heat indices to 105 to 107 degrees. The pattern does begin to change into the weekend as a shortwave moves along the southern edge of the ridge. That will increase moisture and bring a better chance for scattered afternoon showers and storms on Saturday. A few storms could contain strong gusty winds, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours, so have your First Alert Weather App readily available.
If you plan to be in the stands for college football on Saturday, prepare for temperatures in the upper 90s and heat index levels potentially topping 110 degrees inside the stadium. On Sunday through Labor Day, temperatures remain in the 90s with an isolated chance for showers.
